title: Andy Gibson, nicknamed Mouse, and The Hucklebuck
summary: Dance recalls Gibson's rhythm-and-blues work at King Records; Edison says he named Gibson Mouse and that he arranged Hucklebuck.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Well, I mean, there was a thing that -- you know, I knew Andy Gibson fairly well when he was working for King Records and I used to go sometimes when I had some time to waste I used to go around to his office.
Oh, you named him Mouse? You didn't tell me that.

I have a -- see, one of the books I did, I have a review, you know, an interview with him, and -- but you know, he was making these rhythm and blues things and he had Buster Harding, he was helping Buster.
Yeah, right, right. He did a lot of writing for Basie, Buster did.

But you know, Andy would be playing these 45s and he'd say, "That's going to be a hit," and I'd say, "Why? They all sound bad and they all sound alike to me." He said, "What you don't understand is that the kids don't bother too much with what's up front."
Yeah. He wrote "Hucklebuck," you know, Andy Gibson.
* Roy Alfred's tune, lifted from Charlie Parker's riff

He did the arrangement on it and Lucky was playing that long before it became popular. And that was the beginning of a new trend in the music business. The rhythm had changed. But that was strictly black rhythm.
